title: Common dolphin: supplied-model shape, skin and leap revision

sourceAnimation.reason: Artist motion is not a measured individual kinematic recording.

source.sourceTopologyRefined: One Loop subdivision on source body triangles (4:1 refinement); source eyes retained. No primitive replacement body.

source.sourceAttribution: Supplied common-dolphin.zip; no author or licence text embedded. User requested adaptation and publication; no new CC/public-domain grant asserted.

evidence.title: NOAA Fisheries · short-beaked common dolphin
evidence.finding: A sleek beaked body, distinct dorsal fin and tan/grey flank hourglass provide comparative external features. Colour varies with individuals, age and region.
evidence.application: Shape and pigment comparison. The account does not resolve the regional form or subspecies of the private photographs.

evidence.title: Society for Marine Mammalogy · April 2026 list
evidence.read: Current list date and Delphinus taxonomic notes.
evidence.finding: The committee retains a broad common-dolphin concept with provisional regional subspecies and discloses disagreement over eastern Pacific bairdii.
evidence.application: Retain this existing accession and all taxonomy fields; make no new subspecies determination from photographs.

evidence.title: Long, Pabst, Shepherd and McLellan 1997
evidence.read: Author-hosted full PDF; selected Summary, Methods, Table 1 and complete printed p67 Figures 1–2.
evidence.finding: Segment tests from five preserved Delphinus columns demonstrate regional dorsoventral mechanical differences.
evidence.application: Regional bending context. No fitted live waveform, numerical tissue stiffness or natural stroke frequency is transferred to the model.

evidence.title: Weihs 2002 · porpoising dynamics
evidence.read: Publisher abstract and notation; full paper and figures not accessed.
evidence.finding: A theoretical treatment combines leap, coast and active-swimming phases.
evidence.application: Qualitative phase sequence. Energetic motives and parameters are not treated as universal explanations or measurements of this dolphin.

evidence.title: Au, Scott and Perryman 1988 · leap-swim observations
evidence.read: Official NOAA-hosted four-page PDF text and complete first two pages, including Figure 1. Figure 2 is poorly reproduced in the scan.
evidence.finding: Related Stenella observations distinguish leap and underwater segments and separate exit/re-entry splash remnants.
evidence.application: Comparative phase and water-cue context. The reported speeds, distances and uncertain crossover estimates are not assigned to Delphinus or the supplied model.

evidence.title: Dans et al. 2022 · common-dolphin group movements
evidence.read: Retained earlier source review; group-follow scope retained.
evidence.finding: Boat-based group tracks concern spatial movement, rather than individual joint or banking kinematics.
evidence.application: Group-movement context only. The local bank/yaw settings remain authored.

studies.label: Dorsoventral swimming
studies.description: The same skin and geometry bend chiefly in the posterior body; flukes move vertically while lateral span and the forebody stay stable. The 0.8 Hz display cycle, amplitude and envelope are selected, without a measured common-dolphin rate or computed thrust.
studies.evidence: Observed/theoretical biological context; local motion is an authored approximation
studies.timeScale: 12 uncalibrated illustrative seconds; not a measured natural bout

rendering.reason: Regional exterior bending; no individual trajectory or fluid solution.

studies.label: Stroke to glide
studies.description: Finite caudal strokes settle by 5.5 illustrative seconds and hold. Burst/coast theory supplies phase context; display duration, buoyancy and speed are not fitted.
studies.evidence: Observed/theoretical biological context; local motion is an authored approximation
studies.timeScale: 12 uncalibrated illustrative seconds; not a measured natural bout

rendering.reason: Authored transition to a quiet exterior posture.

studies.label: Turning posture
studies.description: A modest whole-body yaw preserves head, eye and appendage attachments and returns to neutral. It is an orientation study, without a solved steering path or forces.
studies.evidence: Observed/theoretical biological context; local motion is an authored approximation
studies.timeScale: 12 uncalibrated illustrative seconds; not a measured natural bout

rendering.reason: Qualitative posture with selected angle and timing.

studies.label: Banked posture
studies.description: A restrained longitudinal bank and yaw accompany local posterior strokes. Group-track observations do not measure these selected bank angles or joint motions.
studies.evidence: Observed/theoretical biological context; local motion is an authored approximation
studies.timeScale: 12 uncalibrated illustrative seconds; not a measured natural bout

rendering.reason: Authored bank and local posterior flexion, not a full maneuver fit.

studies.label: Surfacing study
studies.description: The body rises toward a visible reference water surface, changes pitch, and submerges into a held recovery. The closed external blowhole region crosses the surface. No lung ventilation, spout or respiration rate is calculated.
studies.evidence: Observed/theoretical biological context; local motion is an authored approximation
studies.timeScale: 12 uncalibrated illustrative seconds; not a measured natural bout

rendering.reason: Exterior surface crossing; no respiration or buoyancy model.

studies.label: Jump and re-entry
studies.description: A finite submerged approach and powered exit lead to a parabolic centre path, changing pitch, descent, head-first re-entry and recovery hold. The same body and materials are retained; no underwater thrust is claimed in air. The selected trajectory and illustrative ripples/spray are not fitted from the still photos.
studies.evidence: Observed/theoretical biological context; local motion is an authored approximation
studies.timeScale: 12 uncalibrated illustrative seconds; not a measured natural bout

rendering.reason: Authored trajectory with ballistic flight interval; no fluid/contact/energetic or individual kinematic validation.

limitations: Selected proportions, pigment boundaries, optical values and fine skin detail are unmeasured; no scan, expert certification or numerical biological-accuracy claim.

The jump centre follows an authored parabolic flight interval. Display timing, pitch, stroke amplitude, water ripples and spray are illustrative; no fluid, thrust, contact, respiration or tissue solver.
Broad SMM species concept retained. Private photos are qualitative references, not calibrated individual reconstructions or subspecies determinations.
The mouth remains the supplied closed exterior. Prey capture, jaw intake, echolocation, lung ventilation and internal physiology are not animated.
